summary: BIP 375 per-input shares and proofs, P2TR sender rule, coin selection, full RBF

conventions.txid: display order (reverse of serialized hash), as in BIP 352 vectors

scenarios.title: Proof form: BIP 375 per-input share a_i*B_scan + BIP 374 DLEQ made with that input's key

checks.assert: each share is BIP 375's C = a_i*B_scan (BIP 352 parity applied to the odd-y P2TR key)
BIP 375 VerifyProof(A = input key, B = B_scan, C) accepts each proof
the shares sum to the aggregate share b_scan*A_r (S17, S18): same secret, so every derivation result carries over
the aggregate share's b_scan-witness proof is not a BIP 375 proof (the statement changed, not just the label)
a 'global' share over the receiver's inputs fails BIP 375's 0x07/0x08 check (A_n spans every eligible input)
sender verifies, derives the output itself, applies the amount rule: accepted
the sender's derived output is the receiver's re-derivation, and Bob's restore finds it

scenarios.title: PSBTv0 carriage: BIP 375's per-input layout in PSBT_IN_PROPRIETARY, with BIP 174 length prefixes
scenarios.note: BIP 375 lists PSBT v0 under 'Versions Requiring Exclusion' for 0x1d/0x1e; BIP 174 reserves 0xFC for proprietary use

checks.assert: share key = 27 fc 03 'spj' 1d <B_scan>: 40 bytes incl. the length byte 0x27 (39)
proof key identical but subtype 1e; values are 21||share (34 bytes) and 40||proof (65 bytes)
per receiver input: 179 bytes raw, 240 in base64; ten inputs fit BIP 77's 7,088-byte proposal plaintext many times over
round-trip: the sender parses both pairs and accepts
PDK today strips proprietary pairs on both sides, so the sender sees no share: rejected: no share for eligible input(s) ['bob-tr'] -> Original

scenarios.title: Mailbox-key thief: it can complete a payjoin that pays Bob in full; it cannot redirect, shrink or forge
scenarios.can: read Originals, refuse service, complete payjoins that pay the receiver in full
scenarios.cannot: redirect, shrink, forge a share for the receiver's coins

checks.assert: thief contributes its own coin and takes it back: accepted; Bob's restore finds the full 50,000
redirect to Mallory: the derived output is missing, rejected
shrink Bob's output by 1 sat: amount rule, rejected
a share for Bob's coin made without Bob's input key fails the proof against that input's key
contributing its coin without a proof: rejected (coverage)
an ineligible-only contribution needs no proof, and the output the sender derives still pays Bob in full

scenarios.title: Per-input proofs avoid the ePrint 2026/2037 burn class only with mandatory coverage; this sender check has it
scenarios.remaining: the input-key lie (a false prevout): S27a
scenarios.rule: every eligible input the sender does not own needs a verified share; the sender decides eligibility from the prevouts and hashes every outpoint

checks.assert: sender that sums the shares present derives an output Bob's restore misses (the burn class)
sender check: rejected: no share for eligible input(s) ['bob-b'] -> Original, which Bob's restore finds
a malformed share with no proof check also burns under the naive sender
sender check: the malformed share fails its BIP 374 proof
share made without BIP 352's P2TR negation: proof fails against the input key (a liveness bug, never a burn)
an ineligible receiver input needs no share; the sender still hashes its outpoint (S6g), so the output is found

scenarios.title: What the per-input share tells the sender, under BIP 78 coin choice
scenarios.note: the leak is the same for any BIP 375 co-signer; it is bounded to transactions whose eligible inputs are coins this sender created or was shown

checks.assert: coin c is the output this sender paid Bob earlier
from C_c and t_c the sender extracts the constant b_scan*B_spend
then it finds Bob's unlabelled output in a later solo spend of any coin this sender made
Bob's change on label 0 stays hidden in this one spend (the label tweak needs b_scan; S26f: two such spends reveal it)
a coin it did not create gives only that coin's share, not b_scan*B_spend

scenarios.title: Shares add up: a prober holding the shares of coins it was shown computes the shared secret of any later spend made only of those coins; two such spends with label-0 change give it the label-0 point, after which it finds that change in later such spends
scenarios.note: a coin-adding receiver's mitigation: spend a shown coin only in a payjoin, together with a coin it has not shown, or with non-SP change

checks.assert: each probe session hands the prober one coin's share C_i = b_scan*A_i with a valid proof; it never sees b_scan
one solo spend of a shown coin leaves the label-0 point among 4 candidates
two solo spends, each paying label-0 change: the candidate sets meet in exactly the label-0 point B_spend + L_0*G
a later spend of two shown coins: from C_3 + C_4 alone the prober finds the receiver's unlabelled output (k=0) and its label-0 change (k=1)
the receiver's own scan agrees that those outputs are its own
a spend that includes a coin the prober was not shown: its known shares give the wrong secret, the change stays hidden
one hop only: the change coin's share needs b_scan*B_0, which no probe reveals

scenarios.title: P2TR sender rule: required for contact strings; one-time invoices allow v0 senders, and the residual is a fee-cost burn, never a redirect
scenarios.residual: one-time invoice, sender without a P2TR input: a session-key thief can burn that one payment for a fee; it cannot redirect (plain BIP 77: it could)

checks.assert: contact string, v0-only sender: contact string, no own P2TR input: broadcast the Original
one-time invoice, v0-only sender: the lie passes every check (valid proof for the described key)
BIP 143 digests ignore the other input's prevout, so the real transaction is valid
residual: Bob's restore misses the output, so that one payment is burned
the thief takes its coin back in its own output and pays 300 sat (a fee) to burn it
one-time mode with BIP 77 trust (substitution allowed) lets the same thief redirect the payment
with the proof required, the same redirect is rejected on the one-time invoice too
sender with a P2TR input: checks pass, it signs, and its BIP 341 signature fails against the real prevout
...so the payjoin never confirms and the sender broadcasts the Original, which Bob finds

scenarios.title: No marker carries security: every mode requires the proof; unproven re-derivation only behind a dev flag

checks.assert: one-time invoice: one-time (proof required)
contact string: contact (proof required, own P2TR input)
contact string carrying EX1: contact (proof required, own P2TR input) (S18a's pjv2 sender mode read it as BIP 77 trust)
an invoice the sender saves to pay again is treated as a contact
RK_c thief's substitution to Mallory is rejected whatever the mode (the EX1 redirect is gone)
receiver adds an eligible input without shares: rejected: no share for eligible input(s) ['bob-tr'] -> Original (today's behaviour)
with the dev flag on, the same thief's redirect is accepted (dev flag, unproven: ok): the reason default-on waits for proofs
a receiver without proof support adds nothing; the sender signs the Original's outputs as they are

scenarios.title: Without a mailbox handoff every payment on a contact string shares one mailbox id; the directory's candidate sets
scenarios.assumed: candidate counts and q as in S14a

checks.assert: one payment alone: ~12 candidate txs (3 to 30 across filters), pinned uniquely 15% of the time
two payments on the same mailbox that are linked on chain: pinned 99.8%
two payments with no chain link: both pinned only 2.5% (the mailbox id groups them; it does not pin them)
without a handoff all 12 payments of one contact share one id: the directory always learns their count and timing

scenarios.title: Coin selection is payjoin's open problem: re-offer, chain or fresh; each gives up one property

checks.assert: re-offer: probed coin is the next payjoin's input 83%; 20 probes see 4 coins; 4% of payjoins chain a contact's own coins
chain: probed coin in the next payjoin 0%, probes see 0 new coins, but 100% of payjoins spend that contact's earlier output (an on-chain thread)
fresh: probed coin in the next payjoin 0%, no chaining, but 20 probes see 20 coins and coins run out (30 payjoins of 240)
no option keeps all three properties

scenarios.title: Unspent check: receivers whose invoices or strings an attacker can mint MUST check; interactive ones may skip and limit per string
scenarios.rule: BIP 78: non-interactive receivers need to verify the transaction; interactive ones limit Originals per address

checks.assert: on-demand invoices with no check (S16a's one-time invoice rule): 50 coinless Originals see 7 of 20 coins
on-demand issuer that checks its own node: coinless Originals see 0
with 3 real coins: 2 receiver coins seen, at the cost of 3 real payments (the receiver broadcasts each Original)
interactive contact string (grantee hands one to a funder), no node, per-string limit: 50 probes see 1 coin
an exchange that mints a string per account is on-demand: without the check, 50 accounts see 7 coins

scenarios.title: Full RBF: a payjoin that loses the race can replace the winner; the sender watches until confirmation

checks.assert: B's higher-fee payjoin replaces A's instead of being rejected at broadcast
rule 'if rejected at broadcast, broadcast the Original': A was accepted, then evicted, and is never paid
rule 'watch until it confirms; if it leaves the mempool, broadcast the Original': both paid
the replacement shares exactly one input with the evicted payjoin: anyone logging replacements learns Bob's coin
a receiver that never offers one coin to two live sessions has no race to log

scenarios.title: Leaked string: an sp1 opens no past payment; it lets the holder probe as the contact. An xpub opens the account

checks.assert: leaked account xpub: 17/17 past receipts and change found, and every future one
leaked sp1: 0/12 past SP receipts found without b_scan
leaked contact string: the holder is the contact to the receiver; 30 probes see 1 coin under the per-string limit (its walk-back shows that coin's history, as for any payer)
